label: tier4-cost15-aiv25-n2
_why: THE 2.5x OUTPUT STEP BOOK WITH COST AND ai_value RAISED BACK (user-ruled 2026-09-01). Four changes from the n=7 flat-cost arm 20260831_120102+192428: (1) building_cost vanilla_e0 x 1.5^era (600/900/1350/2030 regular) in place of flat; (2) ai_value 750 x 2.5^era = 750/1875/4688/11719; (3) AI long-construction thresholds 160/240, 4x vanilla 40/60, so the cost ladder does not push the top rung into the penalty band; (4) the whole 2.5-step + scaled-secondaries + era-mapping work of 2026-09-01, which the n=7 arm predates entirely.
_arms: tier4 = {kind: config, config: config/mod_config.tier4.json}, PAIRED tech twin tech_tree_options.tier4.json. -DryRun PASSED lint + negative-goods + solvency 62/62 + TECH CONTENT (193 techs, 0 orphans, 0 duplicate gates) + mod checks + preflight x2. Frozen sha256 A80105162CF6356DDA14E728625B80AF0C8C41B727F6A8337D99585341A1225B. Reproduce the solve with: MOD_CONFIG=config/mod_config.tier4.json INV_IO_CAP=6 INV_MARGINS=0.26,0.41,0.55,0.70 INV_ITERS=1500 node tools/era_inverse.mjs --write. L10 freeze while this runs.
_delta: vs the n=7 flat-cost arm: output step 1.965 -> 2.5 per rung (x7.59 -> x15.6 end to end); per-tier SCALED SECONDARY methods (52 minted across 24 buildings) where they were vanilla-flat; secondaries START at the era maximum except distillery/aeroplanes/tanks; era_game_era [1,3,4,5] so game-era-4/5 methods (radios, rayon, aeroplanes, tanks) are reachable at all; building_cost flat -> 1.5^era; ai_value 750x2.6 -> 750x2.5; thresholds 120/180 -> 160/240.
_predictions: P1 STATED BEFORE THE RUN. GDP falls against the flat-cost n=7 median of 1.39x vanilla, because the frontier is now 3.4x dearer to build end to end. Magnitude NOT predicted - the last cost change moved GDP by more than the cost ratio alone implies, through the capital/GDP loop (F78).
P2 Below-best build share should stay at or below the flat arm 25.2%: the ai_value spread is x15.6 end to end and the frontier is far cheaper to RUN than before, even though it is dearer to build.

P3 The four analytic faults (food loss at 1940; textile, glass, furniture stale) are recipe-book properties and should NOT move with cost or ai_value. If they do, something reads building_cost that should not.

P4 NOT PREDICTED: whether radios and tanks stay on design in game. They clear on design in the SOLVE, but the solve sizes to clear markets and never consults profit - the game does the opposite, so a good produced only by a secondary may still starve.

P5 RISK: the solve has NO profitability constraint on counts (unlike era_scenarios 12 shrink rules), so every scenario figure describes a world where nothing goes out of business. Expect the game to disagree with the seeded scenarios more than the fault count suggests.
_comparison: PRIMARY: the flat-cost n=7 (20260831_120102 + 20260831_192428), same four-rung family. SECONDARY: the n=16 vanilla baseline 20260821_131149. TERTIARY: 20260830_191950 (1.92 cost ladder, n=4). WARNING: different nights, and this arm changes SEVEN things against the n=7 - no single-dial attribution.
_watch: (1) SMOKE-CHECK AT 5 MINUTES on run 1: PM_TECH_REHAUL marker, game version, error.log filtered BY POSITION not by time, clock advancing, queue_mix read WITH the construction sector and GDP beside it (a short queue means it DRAINED). (2) the four restored industries workers vs the n=1 run - the direct read on the fix. (3) below-best share and the per-era build allocation together. (4) PMR_JE| firings. (5) peasant share trajectory, especially the 1875-1880 divergence point where the first x1.4 cost step binds. (6) K trajectory and the 1935 endpoint.
_caveats: n=2. Seven changes move together. The solve behind this book is a FEASIBILITY solve with no loss-shrink, so its scenarios are not equilibria.
